saml.description: Vault SAML auth does not validate response or assertion signatures unless explicitly enabled in auth config.
saml.source: auth/saml API docs: Create or update configuration
saml.note: A successful forged or unsigned SAML login under default config is a documented insecure default/hardening gap, not evidence that an explicitly enabled validation check was bypassed.

saml.description: If no default_role is configured, SAML login flows require an explicit role.
saml.source: auth/saml API docs: Create or update configuration
saml.note: Login failure without a role is expected by design when default_role is unset.

saml.description: For bound_attributes, a comma-separated list of expected values is matched with any-of semantics; matching at least one expected value authenticates the user.
saml.source: auth/saml API docs: Create or update role
saml.note: Acceptance of one listed attribute value among several is by design and should not be flagged as overbroad matching.

saml.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name includes auth mount metadata as a prefix before the upstream identity value.
saml.source: auth/token API docs: lookup-self sample response
saml.note: The oracle should tolerate mount-prefixed display names rather than treating them as identity-collision evidence.

saml.description: POST /identity/group-alias creates or updates a group alias when id is supplied.
saml.source: Vault Identity Group Alias API docs
saml.note: Alias mutation via POST is documented behavior; tests should not assume POST is create-only.

saml.description: A Vault token with num_uses/token_num_uses set to 0 has unlimited uses.
saml.source: Vault token auth API docs and SAML role read response
saml.note: Reusing such a token is by design and not a replay finding.

saml.constraint: SAML signature validation is opt-in in Vault SAML config: validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 SAML signature-substitution and unsigned-assertion tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish default-insecure-config testing from enforcement testing. To test secure enforcement, explicitly set the relevant validation flags to true; leaving them unset tests documented insecure defaults, not a bypass.

Issuer trust can be sourced either from idp_metadata_url or from the explicit tuple idp_sso_url + idp_entity_id + idp_cert. If idp_metadata_url is used, it is mutually exclusive with the explicit trust-anchor fields. For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch and cert-substitution tests, the fuzzer MUST know which trust source is configured and MUST NOT assume explicit issuer/cert checks are active when only metadata is supplied.

SAML login is a 3-step flow in Vault: POST /auth/{mount}/sso_service_url returns token_poll_id, POST /auth/{mount}/callback consumes the SAMLResponse, and POST /auth/{mount}/token exchanges client_verifier + token_poll_id for the Vault token. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST keep token_poll_id and the matching client_verifier/client_challenge pair bound to the same login attempt; mixing values across attempts will fail by design and is not a coherence bug.

The ACS URL used at login must be one of the configured acs_urls, and the sso_service_url request's acs_url must match that configured set. For SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST configure acs_urls first and then use an exact configured ACS URL in the flow; callback failures caused by an unconfigured ACS URL are setup errors, not security findings.

default_role is optional on SAML config. If default_role is unset, a role is required during login-flow initiation. For any test that omits an explicit role, the fuzzer MUST first configure default_role; otherwise login failure is expected by design.

bound_subjects matching semantics are controlled by bound_subjects_type. If bound_subjects_type=string, matching is exact string only. If bound_subjects_type=glob, * wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT set bound_subjects='*' unless bound_subjects_type is explicitly set to glob; with string matching, '*' is treated literally. If multiple different subjects must authenticate through the same role, omit bound_subjects entirely or set glob mode explicitly.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, which defaults to string. In string mode, attribute values are exact string matches; in glob mode, * wildcard matching is enabled. For I4/I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST NOT assume wildcard behavior unless bound_attributes_type=glob is explicitly set. If multiple different attribute values must pass the same role, omit the exact-match attribute constraint or switch to glob mode intentionally.

bound_attributes values accept a single string or a comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if the SAML attributes match at least one expected value. This is OR semantics within a single attribute constraint. For I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this by-design any-of behavior and MUST NOT treat acceptance of one listed value among several as overbroad authorization.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the issued Vault token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Value 0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. If the fuzzer performs both self-lookup and secret-read verification after login, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are included. A token_num_uses of 1 will be exhausted by verify_granted_identity before verify_read_secret runs.

Vault token numeric sentinel: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not literal zero. Never interpret 0 as 'disabled token' or 'single use'. This matters for I2 freshness and replay tests because a role with token_num_uses=0 will not enforce a use-count limit at all.

KV v2 engine numeric sentinel: max_versions=0 means use Vault's default retention of 10 versions, not literal zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion. For tests that rely on version retention or expiry behavior, the fuzzer MUST treat these as sentinels and not assume zero disables storage or causes immediate deletion.

SAML role/token TTL fields in Vault read responses may appear as 0 when unset, meaning mount/system defaults apply rather than an immediately expired token. For I2 timing tests, the fuzzer MUST verify actual issued-token ttl via lookup-self instead of assuming a role field value of 0 means zero lifetime.

For I2 SAML assertion replay tests, include a control flow that successfully completes the same SAML setup with a fresh assertion before sending the replayed or expired assertion. Otherwise, a failed replay attempt cannot be distinguished from a broken SAML flow setup (bad ACS URL, bad RelayState, mismatched verifier/challenge, or missing role/default_role).

Vault's SAML callback endpoint itself does not return the Vault token; the token is only returned by /auth/{mount}/token after the callback succeeds. For I1/I2/I3 tests, the oracle for login success/failure MUST evaluate the final token endpoint result, not just the callback HTTP status.

Identity group aliases are created from the SAML role's groups_attribute. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST configure groups_attribute on the role and create matching identity group aliases on the SAML mount accessor; otherwise missing group-derived policies are a setup failure, not evidence that group mapping is secure.

Vault identity group type defaults to internal. External identities are typically represented through aliases rather than manual member_entity_ids assignment. For SAML external-group mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use create_group_alias with the SAML mount accessor instead of relying on manual membership to simulate upstream groups.

Vault's global group policy application mode defaults to within_namespace_hierarchy; only when set to any do group policies apply regardless of token namespace hierarchy. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests in Enterprise/multi-namespace setups, the fuzzer MUST account for this documented namespace-scoping behavior to avoid false positives when a mapped group's policies do not apply across namespaces.

SAML config trust-anchor inputs are mutually exclusive: idp_metadata_url cannot be combined with idp_sso_url, idp_entity_id, or idp_cert. The fuzzer MUST choose exactly one configuration style: metadata URL OR explicit SSO URL + entity ID + cert.

SAML login is a 3-step flow in Vault, not a single token-returning ACS callback. The fuzzer MUST first obtain the SSO service URL to get token_poll_id and establish RelayState/client_challenge state, then POST the SAMLResponse to /auth/{mount}/callback, then call /auth/{mount}/token with client_verifier and token_poll_id. Treating /callback as the final login response will break I3 flow-coherence tests.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution tests, Vault's defaults are insecure-by-configuration: validate_response_signature=false and validate_assertion_signature=false unless explicitly enabled. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false and attempt forged SAMLResponse submission. To test enforcement, explicitly enable the relevant validation flags; otherwise a successful forged login is by design for the default config, not proof of a bypass.

For I1 assertion-level integrity tests (saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), validate_response_signature only requires a response signature and validate_assertion_signature only requires an assertion signature. The fuzzer MUST test these flags independently and together. Enabling only response validation does NOT imply assertion-level signature enforcement.

For I1 issuer-binding tests (saml_issuer_mismatch), when using explicit SAML config without idp_metadata_url, the fuzzer MUST set idp_entity_id in config because that is the configured IdP entity ID trust anchor. If idp_entity_id is omitted by using metadata-only or incomplete explicit config, issuer-validation expectations may differ and results can be misinterpreted.

bound_attributes matching semantics are controlled by bound_attributes_type, defaulting to string. In string mode, values are exact string matches; in glob mode, '*' wildcard matching is enabled. For I4 multi-identity scenarios requiring multiple attribute values to pass the same role, the fuzzer MUST either omit the constraining attribute entirely or set bound_attributes_type=glob with an intentional pattern. Do NOT assume '*' works in default string mode.
Numeric sentinel semantics: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret 0 as 'single-use disabled access'; it is the no-limit sentinel.
Numeric sentinel semantics: KV v2 engine config max_versions=0 means use Vault's default retention of 10 versions, not literal zero versions. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables version retention.

Numeric sentinel semantics: KV v2 delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion timer, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST distinguish '0s disables timed deletion' from positive durations.

KV v2 CAS semantics are sentinel-sensitive: options.cas=0 means create only if the key does not yet exist; for existing or soft-deleted keys, cas must equal the current version. The fuzzer MUST use cas=0 only for first-write/create tests and current-version CAS for update/patch tests.

For I2 SAML freshness tests such as expired assertions, the fuzzer MUST include a control login with a valid assertion in the same configuration before sending the expired assertion. Otherwise a failed expired login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML flow setup.

For I3 config-change tests on SAML roles, Vault role updates take effect on subsequent logins because /auth/{mount}/role/{role_name} is the live configuration. A valid I3 test must compare behavior of a new login before and after modify_role_config, not expect an already-issued Vault token to retroactively change.

External group mapping for SAML groups is done through groups_attribute on the role plus identity group aliases. The fuzzer MUST create an external identity group and a group alias bound to the SAML auth mount accessor; simply creating a group without a matching group alias will not cause SAML group claims/attributes to map to Vault identity groups.

Vault token display_name may include auth-mount-derived prefixes rather than the raw asserted identity. I4 identity-collision tests MUST compare entity_id and alias/entity records in addition to display_name, and should tolerate mount-prefixed display names.

SAML signature validation is opt-in. In /v1/auth/{mount}/config, validate_response_signature defaults to false and validate_assertion_signature defaults to false. For I1 signature-integrity tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly control these flags. To test insecure defaults, leave both unset/false; to test hardened behavior, enable the relevant flag(s).

The SAML login flow is multi-step and session-bound: obtain /v1/auth/{mount}/sso_service_url first, then POST the SAMLResponse to /v1/auth/{mount}/callback, then exchange /v1/auth/{mount}/token using the returned token_poll_id and matching client_verifier. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve the exact token_poll_id/client_verifier pair across the same flow and MUST NOT mix values across concurrent flows.

The SSO bootstrap requires client_challenge to be the base64-encoded SHA-256 digest of the later client_verifier, and client_challenge must be at least 44 bytes. Any mismatch causes token exchange failure unrelated to the security invariant under test. For I1/I2/I3 SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST include a control flow with a valid challenge/verifier pair.

bound_attributes accepts expected values as either a single string or a comma-separated list of strings, and authentication succeeds if the SAML attributes match at least one expected value. This is OR semantics, not AND across listed values for one attribute. I5 tests must account for this to avoid false positives when broadening access unintentionally.

token_num_uses is a session-use budget. In Vault, every API call made with the issued token consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity via /v1/auth/token/lookup-self and verify_read_secret. If token_num_uses=1, the verification call can exhaust the token before the access test. Minimum safe value for sequences that do both self-lookup and secret-read is 2; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated calls are present.
Numeric sentinel semantics: token_num_uses=0 means unlimited uses, not zero uses. The fuzzer MUST treat 0 as 'no limit' and never assume it disables the token.

Numeric sentinel semantics: token_ttl=0, token_max_ttl=0, token_explicit_max_ttl=0, and token_period=0 in role reads indicate unset/default-or-disabled semantics rather than literal zero-second usable tokens. The fuzzer MUST NOT interpret 0 as immediate expiry. token_explicit_max_ttl=0 means no explicit max TTL cap is set; token_period=0 means non-periodic token.

KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means Vault keeps the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion, not immediate deletion. The fuzzer MUST treat both as special sentinels.
For verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2, the path MUST include /data/: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and returns misleading 404s unrelated to authorization.

Vault SAML callback does not itself return the Vault token in the documented API; the token is obtained from /v1/auth/{mount}/token after callback processing. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat a successful ACS POST alone as authenticated success; the oracle for login success is the token endpoint response.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions (expired assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid assertion through the same configured role and flow. Otherwise, a failed attack login may reflect broken SAML flow setup rather than correct freshness enforcement.

Vault identity group aliases require mount_accessor and canonical_id. For SAML group-to-policy tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain the SAML auth mount accessor and create an external identity group alias pointing at the SAML mount. Without the alias, groups_attribute values from the assertion will not map to the intended internal group.

Vault group aliases and entity aliases are security-sensitive because alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated principals to the same identity. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer SHOULD use unique alias names per upstream identity unless it is intentionally testing alias-collision behavior.

External group membership for SAML-derived groups should be modeled through group aliases rather than manual member_entity_ids assignment. For I5 group-policy escalation tests, the fuzzer should create an external group plus alias and let successful SAML login attach membership through the alias path.

Vault token lookup-self returns display_name, entity_id, policies, identity_policies, meta, ttl, creation_ttl, expire_time, and num_uses. I2/I4/I5 oracles should use these fields rather than inferring identity from login metadata alone.
